The Thonny debugger

A debugger is a slow-motion replay for your code. You can pause on every line and see the value of every variable.

  • Turn on View > Variables. Click an object there to see its attributes.

  • The highlighted line is the one that will run next.

  • Breakpoint: click a line number to put a red dot on it. Press Debug, then Resume: the program runs and pauses at the dot.

A bug-hunting strategy

TipReading an error

Start at the bottom. The last line says what went wrong (TypeError, NameError, IndexError…). The line above it says where: the file and line number.

Weeks 1–5 in one page

Week Remember
1 Git git add then git commit -m "Say what changed"; log, diff, restore.
2 Objects class, __init__, attributes self.x, methods def name(self):.
3 Families class Child(Parent):, super().__init__(…), overriding; “has a” = composition.
4 Searching linear: one by one; binary: sorted list, check the middle, halve.
5 Sorting bubble and selection sort; sorted(key=...); stack (undo) and queue (turns).

New words

debugger
A tool that runs your program in slow motion so you can watch every line and variable.
step over
Run the highlighted line in one go, then pause.
step into
Go inside the function or method that the line calls.
breakpoint
A marked line where the debugger pauses.
traceback
The error report Python prints. Read it from the bottom.
trace table
A paper table where you write each variable’s value, step by step.
